rationale: Interpreted the long-run receipt and closed the short-window limitation of the split-brain chain. Receipt 861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f evaluated all six comparisons: after the healed cluster committed roughly two hundred further entries the feature-on run still had different payloads at the conflict index (violated, witness index 3), the restarted node still reported {A,B,C} (violated, index 3), the run was confirmed substantial and progressing (long_run_exercised and a_log_advanced_after_heal hold, index 3), while the feature-off control run over the same schedule stayed consistent and reported {A,B,C,D,E} (holds, index 8). The child and parent accounts were revised so their "short sampling windows" limitation becomes the observed long run, and the same-term divergence fact gained this receipt as an execution.

knowledge.statement: Two entries that end up at the same log index with the same term but different payloads on different servers are never reconciled by AppendEntries: the receiver truncates its suffix only when an incoming entry at an existing index has a different term, and an entry whose index and term match the stored one is skipped as a duplicate before any configuration or log processing, so the divergence persists while the cluster continues to commit later entries.
knowledge.conditions: AppendEntries conflict handling (raft.go 1526-1553) on a follower whose stored entry at that index has the same term; observed after the split-leader window of the RestoreCommittedLogs restart defect was healed with a further committed entry and, in a later receipt, after roughly two hundred further committed entries.

interpretations.rationale: The two runs differ only in the restart's feature setting and the long run changes nothing about the feature-on outcome. Admissions index 0 and index 5 record the same structural fixture in both modes (snapshot configuration {A,B,C}, committed configuration entry {A,B,C,D,E} above the snapshot, commit index covering it). After the healed leader committed roughly two hundred further entries, the feature-on healed event at index 3 reports entry_consistent_at_conflict_index false and a_config_ids_after_heal {A,B,C}, contradicting both assertions, while its long_run_exercised and a_log_advanced_after_heal operands hold, so the sample is taken after substantial progress and the node is following the leader rather than stalled. The feature-off control at index 8 holds both predicates: entries are consistent and the restarted node reports {A,B,C,D,E}. Mechanism: the same-term entries cannot be reconciled because truncation needs a term difference and duplicates are skipped (raft.go 1526-1553), and the configuration is never refreshed from the committed entry the restart skipped (api.go 610-620 with the replay at 724-753). Limits: the long run is about two hundred entries within one execution rather than a wall-clock long window, it contains no membership change and no snapshot install, and the environment remains in-memory stores with scaled timeouts and a graceful restart.
counterevidence: The feature-off control over the same long run is consistent and reports the committed configuration, so the schedule and the entry volume do not produce the feature-on outcomes.
The progress operand holds, so the persistent stale view is not a symptom of a stalled or isolated node.
limitations: The long run is ~200 committed entries in one execution, not a wall-clock window, and it contains no membership change or snapshot install.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown of the restarted node.
The repair phase that follows still uses harness-arranged lag.

interpretations.rationale: Answer, now including a long run: yes, and the consequences are persistent rather than transient. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay wins an election with fewer votes than the configuration recorded in its own committed log while the other voters elect their own leader, both sides commit at the same index and term, and after the partition is healed the divergent entry and the stale configuration survive roughly two hundred further committed entries with the node following the leader normally (receipt 861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f: entry inconsistency and configuration {A,B,C} persist at index 3 while the progress operands hold, and the feature-off control at index 8 stays consistent). The repair question's receipt 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84 shows what ends it for a node that falls behind: an installed snapshot replaces its log, FSM and configuration. Remaining limits: the long run is entry-count based within one execution and contains no membership change or snapshot install; the repair needs harness-arranged lag; the user Restore and term-changing truncation paths are unexercised; and in-memory stores with scaled timeouts and a graceful restart were used throughout.
counterevidence: The feature-off control run over the identical scenario and long run shows no stale membership, no minority leader and no self-applied write.
The installed-snapshot receipt shows the divergent entry and stale configuration are removed once the node falls behind a compacted leader, so neither is permanent.
The progress operand in the long-run receipt shows the stale view belongs to a node that keeps receiving entries, not to an isolated one.
limitations: The long run is ~200 entries within one execution; no wall-clock window, no membership change and no snapshot install during it.
The repair is per node and needed harness-arranged lag plus a leader snapshot; its operational frequency is not established.
The user Restore path and truncation by a different term are not exercised.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
interpretations.joint_history: Six receipts of five fixed experiments and further revisions over one defect chain: b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e observes the split, 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 adds the healing phase, fa1f90c2eefd45e6af45d7593ac53205 adds applied-state sampling, 112186e8b9544b51b4f7818a04c78a84 (filed under the repair question) adds the repair phase, 531b0a48500843228e26623ce7333943 runs the scenario in both restart modes, and 861a2b3c62bb44d7aed2eee9b95aa15f extends the healed phase into a long run. Compatibility rests on the shared structural fixture in every receipt (snapshot configuration {A,B,C}, a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} above it, a persisted commit index covering it, and the feature-on restarted node reporting {A,B,C}), on identical conflict index 11 and term 3 with minority-write against majority-write in the feature-on receipts, and on the control run reporting {A,B,C,D,E}. Each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt, and each later revision restricted its comparison set to its new predicates, so no receipt is additive evidence for predicates already recorded.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft never rebuilds the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node keeps the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum; that stale view lets it lead with two votes where the current configuration requires three, produces two concurrent leaders whose commits collide at the same index and term, leaves the entry and the applied state different across the cluster, and survives roughly two hundred further committed entries on a healed cluster; an installed snapshot is the observed repair for a node that falls behind, and it also refreshes the stale configuration. Basis: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753); processLogs advances lastApplied (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 610-620) above the committed entry, whereas a restart without the replay scans from the snapshot index and processes it (receipt 531b0a48500843228e26623ce7333943 index 6); quorum and voter admission come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096, 1660-1680); duplicates are skipped so neither the configuration entry nor the conflicting command is reprocessed (raft.go 1526-1553) and the long-run receipt shows that persistence; the persisted commit index exists only because the node ran with the feature enabled (raft.go 1393-1403) and installing a snapshot replaces log, FSM and configuration (raft.go 1935-1972). Remaining limits: the long run is entry-count based with no membership change or snapshot install; the repair needed harness-arranged lag; the user Restore and term-changing truncation paths are unexercised; and in-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown were used. The first filed experiment's receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e remains a retained channel failure with no evaluated comparison.
counterevidence: The feature-off restart control over the identical cluster scenario and long run produces no stale membership, no minority leader and no self-applied write.
An installed snapshot removes both the divergent entry and the stale configuration on that node, so neither is permanent once the node falls behind a compacted leader.
A deployment that never ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled stores commit index 0, in which case the scan covers the entry and no divergence occurs.
limitations: The long run is ~200 entries within one execution; no wall-clock window, no membership change and no snapshot install during it.
The repair is per node and needed harness-arranged lag plus a leader snapshot; its operational frequency is not established.
The user Restore path and truncation by a different term are not exercised.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
interpretations.joint_history: Seven receipts of six fixed experiments over one defect chain: the first constructs the restart state in harness-supplied stores; the second observes the split with state produced by normal operations; the third adds the healing phase; the fourth adds applied-state sampling; the fifth (repair question) adds the repair phase; the sixth runs the scenario in both restart modes; the seventh extends the healed phase into a long run. They share the structural fixture (snapshot configuration {A,B,C}, a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} above the snapshot, a persisted commit index covering it) and the feature-on restart reporting {A,B,C} at the receipt's restart index, with the control run reporting {A,B,C,D,E}. No value is combined across receipts; each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt, and later revisions restricted their comparison sets to new predicates.
